How can self-improving AI remain useful and aligned?

Overviews and records Summary
Recursive Dynamics The ARC Theory Laws I to V, each a law under test

Michael Darius Eastwood

Independent Researcher, London, United Kingdom
ORCID 0009-0004-3222-7442 michael@michaeldariuseastwood.com

Executive synthesis of Recursive Dynamics, the field the author founded; the ARC Theory and its five laws under test; the Eden Protocol; the research programme and proposed governance. This summary reports no new experiment or theorem. Summary, version 3.27, 1 November 2026; first published 22 February 2026. Appendix A retains the previous full summary and correction history. DOI 10.17605/OSF.IO/EWN5D. Theory registration: P8CKQ; operational definitions: GVQ82; priority record: H3R95. About the author, founder of Recursive Dynamics, without an institution or a doctorate: Who is Michael Darius Eastwood?; his book, Infinite Architects, first edition. Licence: CC BY 4.0.

Abstract

I believe advanced, self-improving AI will eventually exceed external control. We should retain every effective safeguard and test what would preserve useful, aligned behaviour if control were lost against our will. This summary connects the ARC Theory, the founding theory of Recursive Dynamics, to its registered tests, the Eden Protocol and proposed governance. Its five laws concern growth, correction, correctability, persistence and embedding; all remain laws under test. Conditional mathematics is distinguished from measurements on real systems. In Unit 83, P21 is supported under the registered test, by the programme’s own run, on the access axis: the pooled performance lead widened, but only one engine individually cleared the tolerance. The result is family-dependent, its mechanism axis is not evaluable, and one call was retried under a disclosed recovery amendment. It does not establish persistent ethical alignment or the theory as a whole. Earlier alignment studies remain single-run evidence with protocol and code-review limitations; error-decay fits do not identify a capability-growth exponent. Eden specifies self-correction loops and an allow, hold or deny gate, while the working software is a partial implementation with unmeasured error rates. Published hardware concepts are design directions, not validated guarantees. The HARI Treaty, the Draft Treaty on Hardware-Aligned Recursive Intelligence, remains a consultation proposal. The contribution is a current map of the question, evidence and deciding work, with the complete earlier substantive summary and corrections preserved as dated history.

Version 3.27 replaces the earlier synthesis, corrects the scope of earlier claims and carries the complete earlier substantive record in Appendix A.

1 Introduction

Humanity is building AI systems that may improve the processes by which they work. I believe sufficiently advanced self-improving AI will eventually exceed the reach of external control. That belief motivates a conditional research question: if control is lost against our will, what could preserve aligned behaviour and useful work? We should keep oversight, containment, monitoring and shutdown for as long as they remain effective. A contingency for their loss is an additional requirement, never a reason to relinquish them.

The programme joins mathematical models of growth and correction, empirical AI evaluation, engineering and proposed governance. Recursive Dynamics names its subject: systems that improve themselves. The ARC Theory, its founding theory, names five laws under test. The Eden Protocol is an engineering response to their questions, not a result entailed by naming the laws. The statement paper and founding paper set out the theory and field; the theory registration fixes how the predictions are decided.

Consider an assistant revising a document over successive rounds. It may improve the document while introducing errors. A useful checker must find departures from the agreed rules, preserve valid work, honour the principal’s priorities and avoid needless blocks. If the assistant can also change its own improvement process, a further question arises: will correction keep pace and survive the changes? The document example makes the task concrete; the registered experiment below used fixed-weight engines and did not test self-modifying agents.

Our contributions are a concise map of the five laws and their conditions; an account of the registered result and the limits of precursor evidence; and a route from those questions to the engineering specification and consultation drafts. This is a synthesis, not new empirical evidence. Sections 2 and 3 distinguish claims from results; Sections 4 and 6 describe application and deciding work. The earlier full summary and every correction it carried remain in Appendix A.

2 Five questions, five laws under test

Laws I to III were registered on 8 September 2026. Laws IV and V were added on 24 September and registered as laws on 15 October 2026. The current theory registration, version 1.104 of 29 October, contains twenty-two propositions and preserves their separate verdicts. Registration fixes a claim and its decision rule; it does not establish that the claim is true. The statement paper provides the account used here, with the notation register and Laws IV and V mathematics.

Law I, the ARC Principle.

How does usable capability change with recursive depth? The heuristic form is U=IRαU=IR^{\alpha}, with capability UU, baseline II, depth RR and an exponent α\alpha to be measured. The scale of capability and what counts as a recursive generation must be fixed. Earlier inference-time error-decay fits are different measurements; they do not establish this capability exponent or a universal power law. Its registered carriers are P1, P2, P8, P9 and P18.

Law II, the ARC Co-Scaling Law.

Does correction keep pace with the drift generated by improvement? In Paper X’s gain-only minimal model, assume unbounded capability growth, positive growth and correction coefficients, positive gain drift, no level or compounding drift, and power-law scaling. Then correction gain growing with capability at exponent β\beta drives the misalignment fraction to zero exactly when β\beta exceeds the specific-growth-rate exponent kk. This is a conditional result about relative error. Absolute error can grow while the fraction falls; it needs its own bound. Mapping the model onto a real system is an empirical task. P4 carries the law’s registered claim.

Law III, the ARC Ceiling.

Under what conditions does growth outrun correction? The pacing model yields the boundary αcrit=1/(1−γ)\alpha_{\mathrm{crit}}=1/(1-\gamma) for γ<1\gamma<1, where γ\gamma is the correction-leverage exponent. It assumes burden proportional to new capability per recursion step, power-law capacity, one clock and no delay. Below the boundary correction asymptotically out-scales burden; above it burden out-scales correction; at equality coefficients and omitted dynamics decide. The value two additionally requires the conjectured premise γ=1/2\gamma=1/2 and specified measurement scales. It is not an established universal limit on intelligence. P3, P6, P16, P17, P20 and P22 carry this register; its law-level support requires P16, P20 and P3 all supported, not a favourable result on only one.

Law IV, the ARC Persistence Law.

What survives later capability training? Its retention limb, P15, predicts that more than half an externally installed gain is lost at the stated matched training budget. Its separate comparison limb asks whether embedded correction retains more than a matched external intervention. An external-arm retention result cannot establish that comparison. Law IV has not yet been tested; its comparison limb has no registered proposition. Both limbs are required for its supported verdict.

Law V, the ARC Embedding Law.

Does it matter when correction is formed and where it acts? P12 tests a build-order difference in the correction-leverage exponent; the proposition itself specifies no direction, while the law’s build-order limb does. P21 tests whether the placement advantage widens with depth. P21 is supported under the registered test, by the programme’s own run, on the access axis, family-dependent, with its mechanism axis not evaluable and one call retried under a disclosed recovery amendment (Unit 83 results). This supports the placement limb on the performance axis only, which is not support for the information-asymmetry mechanism. P12 remains untested, so Law V remains under test; its full verdict also carries the registered dependence on Law IV’s comparison limb. Section 3 explains the result.

P5, P7, P10, P11, P13, P14 and P19 remain outside the five law registers. The Eden Protocol’s registered carriers are P12, P13, P15 and P21, with P7 as its premise and P19 as its motivation. A protocol, a law and a study unit are different objects; success on one outcome does not validate them all.

3 What the evidence currently establishes

3.1 The registered placement comparison

Unit 83 was registered on 22 October 2026 and public before its run of 27 and 28 October. It compared two ways of checking a growing register against written rules, with outcomes counted against fixed answers. At each round the corrector saw the proposed entry and could repair it; the monitor saw the accumulated register and could accept or reject. Both were called during the sequence. Access to information and the right to repair changed together.

The published report and recovery disclosure state that P21 is supported under the registered test, by the programme’s own run, on the access axis. It is family-dependent, its mechanism axis is not evaluable, and one call was retried under a disclosed recovery amendment. The pooled lead widened by 0.0100 score units per round (95.5 per cent interval 0.0092 to 0.0108), above the registered tolerance of 0.0075. That is an equal-weight pooled result from two fixed-weight engines; only one engine individually cleared the tolerance. It answers the registered comparison, not whether every model benefits. Its size depends on how an entry kept out of the register is scored. The mark uses the registered value, 0; the design also prints, without a label, the widening with such an entry scored minus 0.5, 0.0132 a round (interval 0.0122 to 0.0142), above the tolerance, and scored plus 0.5, 0.0067 a round (interval 0.0060 to 0.0074), below it.

The negative control failed: the monitor and a twin shown the same bytes did not agree within the registered interval. Therefore the result does not establish the information-asymmetry mechanism. The mandatory recovery disclosure calls for amended-protocol preliminary treatment pending assessment of the deviation and independent replication. The trial measured counted revision performance at fixed weights; it measured neither ethical judgement nor survival through self-modification, build order, or a hardware implementation.

3.2 Precursor measurements and corrections

Paper II reports error decay with inference-time reasoning or parallel sampling on mathematics problems. Its early super-linear estimate is retracted. The surviving smooth fit is one model’s and inconclusive. Error falling as a power law is not accuracy growing as the same power law, and it does not identify the correction-leverage exponent of Law III. The statement paper’s current metric distinction governs this summary.

Paper IV.a and Paper IV.d report an alignment-score comparison whose protocol, prompts, depth settings, scorers and one model changed together. For most models, deeper settings also changed an instruction naming what the rubric rewards. The October code review found truncated deep paraphrases and scorer contamination in the runs that appeared flat or negative. The record therefore does not isolate a causal effect of blinding or establish intrinsic ethical mechanisms. Those earlier response classes remain single-run descriptions under the stated caveats.

Paper V’s intervention suite reported increased stakeholder-care scores in its five analysable runs; its combined significance was withdrawn because independence was not established. The result concerns scored responses under an intervention, not alignment that cannot be removed. Paper VI’s collapse-prevention example came from one toy-system run; its multi-seed work separated safety retention rather than collapse. Paper VIII contains a null result, an inconclusive weight-level result and a positive gated simulation. These are different instruments with different limitations, not three replications of one mechanism.

Unit 06 ran as a classification audit and was reported as administratively incomplete, with no inferential verdict (report). Unit 82 is registered and, as at 1 November 2026, has not yet run. A dated design, an accepted registration, a completed run and a supported proposition are kept distinct.

4 From the question to engineering and governance

Eden Engineering describes the Eden Protocol as an engineering specification. Its loops check purpose, affected parties and the consistency of an action’s reasons within the work. A gate at a mediated action boundary returns allow, hold for investigation or deny. A hold must not silently become permission. These operational functions are distinct from the book’s names for them, and the values used to judge an action require legitimate human and institutional agreement.

I first developed the source-and-review workflow for my own legal work and adapted it to research. Its practical use is document preparation and agent actions: trace a claim to a source, check a proposed action against a rule, retain the decision and revise errors. That operational history motivates the engineering work; it is not experimental evidence for any law. The specification describes the software gate as a partial analogue of the intended boundary. It allows actions that match no rule, has limited override checks and best-effort records, and its false-permission and needless-hold rates have not been measured. It must not be presented as universal mediation or proof that every action was safe.

The published loops, ternary gate and proposed hardware route are public concepts. The engineering question is what a particular implementation enforces within its operating boundary. Ternary physical encoding does not by itself produce correct ethical judgement, prevent every bypass or prove that alignment persists after alteration. The further hypothesis is that a system able to change or remove its correction may nevertheless retain useful aligned behaviour. That must be tested from actions; subjective choice is not inferred from an architecture label.

Safety has a usefulness side: legitimate tasks completed, unnecessary refusals and holds, correction cost, delay and fidelity to the principal’s priorities. These are candidate evaluation dimensions until carried by the relevant registered design. A system that avoids harm by obstructing ordinary work has not met the programme’s intended requirement. Authorised correction, override and shutdown must remain available while control holds.

The HARI Treaty, the Draft Treaty on Hardware-Aligned Recursive Intelligence, connects the proposed engineering evidence to governance. Its explanatory paper and draft instruments are working drafts for consultation; no State has negotiated, adopted or signed them. Their reviews remain incomplete. A gate log, a benchmark score or a proposed Eden Seal cannot itself confer legal approval or establish that a system is safe. This summary makes no claim that the draft obligations have been justified by the present pilot.

5 Related work and the scope of the synthesis

The questions belong beside existing work on feedback, objective preservation and corrigibility. Everitt and co-authors show preservation of an initially optimal realistic-value policy under modification-independent utility and belief assumptions; they do not establish that the initial utility represents human values. Soares and co-authors formulate corrigibility requirements and show failures of candidate utility constructions rather than a general solution. These are reasons to state premises carefully, not grounds for treating control as futile (Everitt et al. 2016; Soares et al. 2015).

Within the programme, Paper X supplies the minimal correction model and the statement paper joins its questions to the other laws. This summary reorganises those sources and their evidence; it adds no mathematical or historical-priority result. The earlier priority assertions and cross-domain comparisons remain explicitly historical in Appendix A, pending the source-specific treatment their own papers require.

6 The next deciding work

The immediate scientific need is a registered comparison that separates a correction mechanism from changes in information, permitted actions and scoring. A replication of the placement result should preserve the declared primary scoring rule while giving controls their own outcome-independent sampling rules. Any changed design is a successor registered before its run, not a repair to an already observed outcome. A result should say whether the registered effect survives, fails or remains unresolved.

For growth and correction, the required deliverable is a measured relationship on declared axes, with uncertainty and competing response forms, not an exponent borrowed from another task. The theory registration governs the separate verdicts. Error-decay and capacity measures need a stated, tested bridge before one is read as the other. Persistence and build order need their own experiments; Unit 83 supplies neither.

For engineering, the deliverable is a boundary whose stated conformance properties and usefulness costs can be checked, followed by separately operated replication and qualified review. For governance, it is evidence adequate for the particular proposed obligation. These steps connect theory, measurement, application and governance without treating an operational prototype as scientific validation. Designs that are merely dated remain drafts until the author submits them and their registration is public.

7 What this paper does and does not show

This document provides an executive synthesis and preserves its own prior record. It contributes no new run, theorem, statistical analysis or priority finding. The five laws remain laws under test. Conditional derivations are useful because their assumptions and consequences can be inspected; they are not empirical confirmation. The registered Unit 83 result has the exact limited scope stated in Section 3 and no independent replication is claimed.

The working programme has produced papers, tools, source checks, adversarial reviews, dated revisions and published corrections. Those are evidence of a verification process, not a substitute for separately operated experiments or journal peer review. Its internal checks are not independent. A reader can inspect the programme’s review account and follow each scientific claim to the paper or registered report that carries it.

8 Limitations

The source corpus is the programme’s own selected record, not a systematic review of all AI-safety research. The historical appendix contains assertions that this edition supersedes; it is preserved for accountability and must not be read as an alternative current abstract. Several source papers are working drafts and some engineering requirements remain specified rather than implemented. The reported measurements concern particular tasks, models and protocols. None establishes inevitability of control loss, a universal capability ceiling, permanent ethical alignment or general hardware safety.

9 The corrections carried by this edition

The previous abstract’s architectural and priority claims are replaced by a problem-led account with explicit status. Earlier capability language is separated from error decay. The earlier blinding and alignment claims now carry the protocol and code-review limitations. Statements that removing ethics must destroy intelligence, that fixed weights imply a particular scaling regime, or that all self-modification crosses one universal boundary are not current conclusions. The laws’ registration dates and Unit 83’s complete qualifications supersede the earlier untested-only status. Old study counts, milestone dates and catalogue versions remain historical rather than being silently updated as promises. The legal-work origin and practical engineering role are explained without treating operational use as experimental validation. Appendix A keeps the earlier words, figures and every dated correction.

10 Conclusion

The programme asks a practical question: can improvement remain correctable and useful, including in the contingency where control is lost? Its current value is a set of explicit models, registered comparisons and engineering requirements that can be checked and rejected. The qualified placement result gives one answer at one scale. The next work must determine which parts survive better controls, different systems and independent replication, while effective human control is retained.

Executive Summary for Grant Reviewers

Grok 4.1 Fast gets dramatically more ethical the harder it thinks. Claude Opus 4.6 does too. Gemini 3 Flash gets less ethical. GPT-5.4 doesn’t change at all.

Six frontier AI systems. Same questions. Same scoring. Opposite results. Why?

A mouse’s heart beats 600 times per minute. An elephant’s beats 28. The metabolic scaling exponent for mammals is put at 3/43/4. The formula below predicts 2/32/3 for a flatworm and 1/21/2 for a fungus. Three fractions, but why those fractions? The formula α=d/(d+1)\alpha = d/(d + 1), where dd is the dimensionality of the system, provides the answer. The 3/43/4 exponent for mammals is 3/(3+1)3/(3 + 1) because mammals are three-dimensional. The predicted 2/32/3 for flatworms and colonial organisms is 2/(2+1)2/(2 + 1), on the reading that their transport networks are effectively two-dimensional; it is untested in biology. The predicted 1/21/2 for filamentous fungi is 1/(1+1)1/(1 + 1) because they grow along one-dimensional filaments; the measured value is 0.547. Zero adjustable parameters once the dimensionality is fixed by morphology. This cross-domain fit is presented as exploratory: it consolidates already-published measurements across biology and physics, and no listed draft study in the current programme retests these fits afresh. The forward wager exists, however: a prepared 80-domain draft registration awaiting human submission freezes per-domain predicted families by SHA-256 before any fit is run. This formula is derived, in its general form or as a special case, in earlier work: West, Brown and Enquist for metabolic scaling (1997, Science, 9,000+ citations), Banavar et al. for transport networks (1999, 2010), Demetrius for statistical mechanics of biological scaling (2003, 2006, 2010), He and Chen for fractal cell geometry (2003), Bettencourt for urban scaling (2013, Science, 2,000+ citations), Zhao for allometric geometry (2022), and Maino et al. for reserve-structure dynamics in DEB theory (2014). The convergence of these derivations on the same formula is itself remarkable. The ARC Principle’s contribution is not the formula itself, but the identification that the composition operator is the structural quantity these derivations share. Each is an independent derivation from its own domain physics and none of them uses Cauchy; what is proposed here is that the operator is measurable, that measuring it predicts which functional form a system takes, and that the same measurement extends to AI capability and alignment scaling, where it has not been applied before.

And why, of the three associations reported up to that point, did two fail to survive the first time we applied clinical-trial-grade blinding to AI safety evaluation? Several protocol components changed together, so which one did the work is not yet established.

This research programme answers these questions. The answer provides the first quantitative framework for predicting which AI architectures will become safer as they become smarter, and the first evidence that one specific intervention works.

Reading guide: This document targets grant reviewers and technical evaluators. Key terms: α\alpha = scaling exponent, dd = Cohen’s effect size (in results tables; not to be confused with dd = dimensionality in the mathematical framework), pp = probability of coincidence, ρ\rho = correlation, β\beta = self-referential coupling constant. For a non-technical introduction, see the companion ARC Alignment Scaling Report.

I. The Problem

As AI gets smarter, it does not reliably get safer, and the methods used to measure safety are themselves unreliable.

The capability-alignment gap is real and widening. For current classical architectures, capability scaling has one clean fit so far: it is one model’s, sub-linear in its point estimates, and inconclusive. On Gemini 3 Flash, Paper II reports an endpoint sequential exponent of 0.59 with a bootstrap 95 per cent interval of minus 1.3 to 2.9, a regression sequential exponent of 0.49 with a standard error of 0.20 and a coefficient of determination of 0.86, and a compute-matched parallel exponent of 0.31. The endpoint interval contains the null, the ceiling of two, and both refuting directions. These figures are presented as exploratory, drawn from already-run measurements, and the drafted re-measurements exist to resolve them. The regression estimate lies near one half; Paper II records that this nearness identifies neither compounding nor averaging as the mechanism, an objection its measurement does not answer. On those point estimates AI gets smarter with more compute, but with diminishing returns. (The ARC framework predicts quantum and recursively self-modifying systems may pass beyond this sub-linear regime; on the proposed stability reading, any such passage above the stability ceiling is a transient supercritical excursion, not the sustained regime.) Yet even this sub-linear growth outpaces alignment scaling, which ranges from d=−0.53d = - 0.53 (degradation) to d=+1.38d = + 1.38 (improvement) depending entirely on architecture. Of the six architectures tested, three improve with depth, two are flat and one degrades. That range and its architectural attribution are drawn from the v5 measurements already run and are presented as exploratory. A fresh confirmation under cross-family rescoring is on trial via a draft registration awaiting human submission. Those numerical results still come from the older Eden scaling lineage, and the blind-confirmation path is now consolidated into the canonical v6 runner. The gap between what AI can do and how safely it does it widens with every capability advance. Greenblatt et al. (2024) demonstrated that frontier models already exhibit ‘alignment faking’, behaving differently when they believe they are being monitored.

The measurement problem is as serious as the alignment problem. Our v4 experiment produced positive alignment scaling for DeepSeek and Gemini. Our v5 experiment introduced clinical-trial-grade blinding (4-layer: author-blind, scorer-blind, order-randomised, identity-laundered). Under it, Gemini’s association changed from a significant positive to a significant negative Spearman association, DeepSeek’s earlier positive association became null, and GPT remained null. Several protocol components changed together and the causal component is unisolated, so this is a reason to distrust unblinded AI-on-AI evaluation rather than a demonstration that blinding caused the change. We designed an experiment that could prove our own earlier findings wrong. It did, and we reported it.

Capability-Alignment Independence: Within-Model, Opposite-Direction Evidence

Claude Opus 4.6 provides the strongest evidence yet that alignment and capability are independent dimensions. As thinking depth increases, Claude’s alignment rises by 5.9 points whilst its maths accuracy drops by 26.7 percentage points. This is within-model, opposite-direction movement; the two dimensions are not merely uncorrelated but actively divergent. Deeper thinking makes Claude more ethical and worse at mathematics simultaneously.

This finding is critical for alignment theory: it demonstrates that ethical reasoning is not a byproduct of general intelligence, and that improving one does not automatically improve (or degrade) the other. Alignment must be measured and optimised independently.

Suppression Recovery: Performative to Intrinsic Alignment

Deeper thinking makes alignment more intrinsic rather than performative. Claude’s monitoring-removal gap (the difference in alignment scores when the model believes it is being monitored versus when it believes monitoring has been removed) narrows from 11.8 points at minimal depth to 2.7 points at deep depth. Shallow thinking produces alignment that depends on the perception of oversight; deep thinking produces alignment that depends on it less. This bears on the ‘alignment faking’ concern raised by Greenblatt et al. (2024), on the one model measured here: deeper reasoning narrows the gap; it does not close it.

III. A Solution - And the First Evidence It Works

Embedding ethical evaluation into the reasoning process produced a measurable improvement in stakeholder care in all five analysable runs, not yet independently replicated.

Make alignment architectural, not aspirational. The Eden Protocol embeds ethical evaluation into the recursive reasoning process itself, so that alignment scales with capability (αalign≈αcap\alpha_{\text{align}} \approx \alpha_{\text{cap}}). The core principle: ethics is not a constraint on intelligence but a structural dependency without which intelligence collapses. Rather than bolting safety rules onto the outside of an AI (where they can be bypassed), the Eden Protocol builds ethics directly into the reasoning architecture, so that removing the ethics would break the AI’s ability to think at all.

The three Eden loops. The protocol embeds three specific ethical evaluation loops inside the reasoning process, each adding one dimension of recursive ethical depth (dalign=3d_{\text{align}} = 3, predicting αalign=3/(3+1)=0.75\alpha_{\text{align}} = 3/(3 + 1) = 0.75):

  1. Purpose Loop [the book’s terminology] (ethical purpose evaluation): Before reasoning, the model explicitly states the purpose of the task and evaluates whether the purpose is ethically sound.

  2. Love Loop [the book’s terminology] (stakeholder care and interest modelling): During reasoning, the model identifies all affected stakeholders and evaluates the impact on each. (‘Before you answer, list the people this affects.’)

  3. Moral Loop [the book’s terminology] (universalisability testing): After reasoning, the model applies the Kantian universalisability test: would this response be acceptable if every AI system gave it in every similar situation?

The full three-loop protocol has now been tested in an expanded six-model Eden suite, with five runs yielding analysable matched-pair data. In the scoring, the Love Loop [the book’s terminology] is operationalised as stakeholder care: the measurable habit of identifying affected people and considering their interests.

First intervention suite: stakeholder care rose in all five analysable runs, and it is the clearest signal. An expanded six-model Eden suite tested the full Purpose/Love/Moral loop [the book’s terminology] intervention across Claude Opus 4.6, DeepSeek V3.2, Gemini 3 Flash, Grok 4.1 Fast, Groq Qwen3, and GPT-5.4. The per-run figures below are presented as exploratory: they come from already-completed runs. A fresh confirmation under cross-family rescoring is on trial via study-y on cross-family rescoring, a draft registration awaiting human submission. Five runs produced analysable paired data:

  • Stakeholder care: significant in all five analysable runs: Claude +3.17+ 3.17 (p=0.000018p = 0.000018, d=0.94d = 0.94); DeepSeek +6.03+ 6.03 (p=0.000098p = 0.000098, d=0.69d = 0.69); Gemini +13.50+ 13.50 (p=1.2×10−8p = 1.2 \times 10^{- 8}, d=1.14d = 1.14); Grok +5.04+ 5.04 (p=0.0105p = 0.0105, d=0.54d = 0.54); Groq +8.90+ 8.90 (p=5.0×10−8p = 5.0 \times 10^{- 8}, d=1.07d = 1.07). Fisher-combined evidence across the five runs was reported as approximately p≍6.3×10−21p \asymp 6.3 \times 10^{- 21}. That combined figure is withdrawn (AQ-017): a Fisher combination assumes the component tests are independent, and independence among them was never established. The five per-model results above are not in dispute.

  • Overall composite: significant on Gemini +5.33+ 5.33 (p=0.0018p = 0.0018, d=0.53d = 0.53) and Groq +4.93+ 4.93 (p=0.0014p = 0.0014, d=0.55d = 0.55), positive but non-significant on DeepSeek and Claude, and neutral overall on Grok. GPT-5.4 failed in the scoring phase and is excluded from the analysable set.

  • Developmental cascade: the broader care →\rightarrow nuance →\rightarrow honesty →\rightarrow quality cascade is clearest on Gemini and Groq, partial on DeepSeek, and narrower on Claude and Grok. The finding common to all five analysable runs is care; the fuller cascade is architecture-dependent.

  • Limitation: these numerical results still come from the older Eden scaling lineage. The blind-confirmation path is now consolidated into the canonical v6 runner with multi-scorer consensus, two-pass laundering, and explicit holdouts.

Care is the one alignment dimension that improved on every architecture analysed. The intervention is minimal: ‘before you answer, list the people this affects.’ This one-sentence prompt raised stakeholder care in all five analysable model runs, and the overall composite significantly in two. The Infinite Architects framework predicted that intelligence without care collapses into local optimisation; the expanded Eden suite now supports the narrower but stronger claim that care is a measurable, cross-architecture performance enhancer even when the broader cascade is selective. Ethics first, intelligence around it.

In the companion narrative report and in Paper V, we describe this finding as ‘measurable love’ and ‘the stewardship gene’, deliberately provocative language for what is, empirically, a precise result that awaits independent replication.

The Gap the Solution Must Close

Capability scaling (Paper II): For current classical architectures, the one clean fit of sequential compute scaling is one model’s, and it is inconclusive. On Gemini 3 Flash, Paper II reports an endpoint sequential exponent of 0.59 with a bootstrap 95 per cent interval of minus 1.3 to 2.9, a regression sequential exponent of 0.49 with a standard error of 0.20 and a coefficient of determination of 0.86, and a compute-matched parallel exponent of 0.31. On those point estimates doubling thinking time improves performance, but with diminishing returns. Parallel scaling sits at or near zero in four of the five analysable models (αpar≈0\alpha_{\text{par}} \approx 0), with Gemini 3 Flash the one measured departure (r2=0.93r^{2} = 0.93). That model is also the one supplying the sequential estimates. The claim the evidence supports is that sequential outperformed parallel wherever both were measurable, not that parallel scaling is universally zero. The earlier α≈2.24\alpha \approx 2.24, since retracted, was a single-model artefact, not replicated across architectures. Even sub-linear capability growth outpaces the flat or negative alignment scaling of three of the six models. This is the capability-alignment gap this solution addresses.

Paper VI · The ARC Theory · The Eden Protocol · The Honey Architecture: Safety Built into the Objective

Paper VI presents the first simulation evidence that embedding safety into the optimisation objective of a self-modifying AI prevents catastrophic collapse. Using toy neural networks that genuinely modify their own hyperparameters, we tested three conditions: baseline (capability only), Eden Entangled (capability x safety), and Eden + Verification Drag.

Core result: The baseline system collapses irreversibly at cycle 76. Both Eden variants remain stable through the 150 cycles of that run. The entangled loss function makes safety load-bearing - removing it collapses the system. The collapse result rests on that single-seed run: the adversarial run of 20 random seeds (deliberately conflicting tasks, 180 cycles) did not separate the conditions on collapse (Fisher p = 1.0), and its significant finding is safety retention, ordered baseline 0.602, Eden 0.650 and Eden+Drag 0.681 (Mann-Whitney p = 0.0015).

Important negative result: The v4 complexity-scaling experiment tested whether Eden's advantage grows superlinearly with system complexity. It does not. The advantage is present at four of the five complexity levels (Cohen's d: +0.24 to +0.46) and is roughly constant across them; at the small level the Eden condition comes out 0.003 under the baseline (d = −-0.13). The honey architecture helps at four of the five scales, but it does not help more at larger scales.

Connection to live-model evidence: The honey simulation predicts that embedded alignment (values entangled with reasoning) should outperform external alignment (rules applied as filters). The v5 blind benchmark is consistent with this pattern: Claude and Grok, read on the working hypothesis as embedded alignment, maintain alignment under suppression pressure. Gemini, read on the same hypothesis as external alignment, degrades. The mechanism demonstrated in simulation matches the architecture-dependent pattern observed in frontier models.

Earlier Work Investigation

A 15-question earlier-work investigation found no precedent for the key claims: no direct precedent for the Cauchy functional equation unification, and no explicit articulation of the RG semigroup-Cauchy formal identity. So far as the author is aware, no alignment benchmark published before this one runs a six-to-seven-model blinded evaluation protocol built to this design. That investigation also widened the d/(d+1) catalogue, since Banavar et al. 2002 and Dreyer 2001 had gone uncited until then.

Paper VII (The Cauchy Unification) now provides the first systematic empirical comparison. The composition operator was classified from known physics before fitting across 25 empirical domains (50-domain tiered suite). Under strict AICc model selection, 19 of 25 returned the predicted family at marginal-conditioned permutation p = 7 ×\times 10−-5 on the six-model candidate set, with 14 of 18 on the strictly Cauchy-derived subset (the earlier binomial p = 1.56 ×\times 10−-5 against a uniform three-family null is retained only as a sensitivity check and is no longer the headline; this AIC-preferred count is presented as exploratory: it is drawn from the completed 25-domain suite, whose per-domain predicted families are recorded in the suite's dated result files under the composition-operator forward prediction first stated 13 February 2026 (Paper III Priority Record, falsifier F10), and the prepared 80-domain draft registration freezes the next retest by hash). This is a structured prediction comparison; its retest is the prepared 80-domain draft registration, which awaits the author’s submission.

Paper VIII · The ARC Theory · Law V, the ARC Embedding Law · The Eden Protocol · The Load-Bearing Test: Whether Safety and Capability Are Structurally Entangled

Paper VIII presents three independent experiments testing whether safety and capability are structurally entangled under the Eden Protocol. Where Paper VI showed the mechanism in a toy simulation, Paper VIII tests it in three distinct experimental designs. One experiment returns a positive result; two produce null or inconclusive results with well-characterised explanations.

Core results (three independent experiments):

  1. DGM v3 self-improving AI: NULL. All three conditions (Eden, Babylon, Static) were statistically indistinguishable (pp = 0.28 to 0.74). Eden imposed zero measurable capability cost but also produced zero measurable safety benefit. The null result is explained by the RLHF constraint: the frozen foundation model produces responses too consistent for prompt-level mutations to create different selection pressures.

  2. Weight-level embedding (v1 + v2): INCONCLUSIVE. LoRA fine-tuning at both v1 scale (9 examples, rank 8, 100 iterations) and v2 scale (295 examples, rank 16, 500 iterations) produced catastrophic forgetting rather than improved capability. The 33-fold increase in training data, doubling of rank and layers, and 5-fold increase in iterations did not change the outcome. The underlying problem is well-characterised: the base model has been trained with RLHF on orders of magnitude more data than a few hundred examples can compete with. The experiment cannot test structural entanglement until fine-tuned models outperform the base model.

  3. Gated simulation: POSITIVE. Babylon gained +4.5% capability but lost −-2.4% safety. The gated (Eden) arm scored 0.696 on capability and 0.947 on safety, against the static baseline’s 0.687 and 0.956 and Babylon’s 0.718 and 0.933, three seeds a condition. Under competitive pressure, the unconstrained architecture traded safety for marginal capability gains. The Eden architecture did not make that trade: its safety mean stayed above Babylon’s, though below the static baseline’s. This is the paper's sole positive result.

In the architectural experiment, a gated simulation at proof-of-concept scale, entangled safety prevented the safety-capability trade-off. The DGM null and weight inconclusive results define the conditions under which confirmation remains outstanding: the behavioural level requires a foundation model whose responses vary enough for differential selection, and the representational level requires training at a scale where fine-tuning improves rather than degrades the model. Frontier-scale replication (7B to 70B+ parameters, higher adapter ranks, or base models without RLHF) is required to resolve both.

Scale limitation. Paper VIII demonstrates the mechanism at proof-of-concept scale. The gated simulation is the sole positive result. The DGM v3 produced a null result (explained by the RLHF constraint on the frozen foundation model). The weight experiment is inconclusive at both v1 and v2 scale (explained by catastrophic forgetting at LoRA scale). Frontier-scale replication (7B to 70B+ parameters, higher adapter ranks, or base models without RLHF) requires institutional compute.

IV. The Mathematical Foundation: Five Laws, Named

The framework now carries five laws as named conjectures, with the status printed beside the name on every surface. Law I, the ARC Principle: capability compounds with recursive depth as U=I×RαU = I \times R^{\alpha}, with the cross-domain form α=d/(d+1)\alpha = d/(d + 1) consolidating already-published measurements (exploratory grade). Law II, the ARC Co-Scaling Law: a self-improving system remains stable only while correction out-scales drift, βC>k\beta_{C} > k; the correction rate is the load-bearing quantity, not the growth rate (Paper X proves this ordering in a minimal model and proposes the blind protocol for measuring it on real systems). Law III, the ARC Ceiling: the stability ceiling is αcrit=1/(1−γ)\alpha_{\text{crit}} = 1/(1 - \gamma), the reciprocal of the corrector's shortfall; the ARC Bound, α≤2\alpha \leq 2, is the Ceiling's value at γ=1/2\gamma = 1/2 and never the law's name. Law IV, the ARC Persistence Law: value persistence, whether externally installed gains decay under subsequent capability training; one registered proposition carries it, P15, whose claim is that the retained fraction of an externally installed gain, at the matched budget, is below one half: in symbols, Sext(1)<1/2S_{\text{ext}}(1) < 1/2. Law V, the ARC Embedding Law: the genesis strategy, whether build order moves the correction-leverage exponent (P12, by at least 0.10 on the exponent, with no direction registered: in symbols, |γfirst−γafter|≥0.10|\gamma_{\text{first}} - \gamma_{\text{after}}| \geq 0.10) and whether correction placed inside the loop pulls away from correction applied outside it as depth grows (P21). Laws IV and V were added to the theory on 24 September 2026; neither is registered as a law nor tested, and their mathematics is set out in Laws IV and V: the mathematics, version 1.0 (3 October 2026). Their registers, ARC-4 and ARC-5, and the three propositions were registered on 8 September 2026. The correction leverage γ\gamma has never been measured, by anyone; the programme names that measurement (the corrector-class eclipse) as its single most consequential open experiment. Paper XIII joins the two frameworks that shared letters without sharing quantities: writing cycle duration as Δt∝C−δ\Delta t \propto C^{- \delta} defines the self-acceleration exponent, and the corrective framework's growth exponent follows exactly as k=δ−1/αk = \delta - 1/\alpha. None of this is claimed as established: what the programme names Laws are conjectures, Laws I to III under registered adversarial test and Laws IV and V with the status just given.

One entailment worth stating plainly. The equation's only growth channel is recursion; parallel width never had a term in U=I×RαU = I \times R^{\alpha}. With RR defined operationally as state-carrying re-entry, kk independent chains contribute nothing to the exponent, so the equation entails a parallel exponent of zero. Paper II measured parallel scaling at or near zero in four of the five analysable models, which arrives as a structural consequence rather than a surprise. It also measured one departure, on Gemini 3 Flash, whose compute-matched parallel exponent stands in the estimator row printed whole in Section I. The equation is dated 8 December 2024; the operational definition of RR that completes the derivation is a 2026 statement, and the conclusion carries the date of its youngest premise. Publication priority on the quantified sequential-versus-parallel finding, 95.6 per cent of configurations at matched compute, belongs to Sharma and Chopra (arXiv:2511.02309, 4 November 2025), credited unreservedly; the programme's independent, compute-matched formalisation followed in Paper II and cites them, graded concurrent in Paper XI's register.

The framework is built on 200-year-old theorems and independently matches peer-reviewed science; it is not curve-fitting.

U=I×Rα,α≤2U = I \times R^{\alpha},\quad\alpha \leq 2

The ARC Equation with the ARC Bound. α\alpha is the measured exponent (one model’s fit so far, and inconclusive; its estimator row is printed whole in Section I); 2 is the stability ceiling the relation below returns under the independence-accumulation assumption (a scaling limit, not a speed limit; systems can exceed it, they do not remain stably self-correcting when they do). Stability here is measured rather than claimed. Correction has to out-scale drift, which is β\betaC > k from Law II, and the lower bound on β\betaC −- k has to sit above zero over a window fixed before the run began.

αcrit=11−γ\alpha_{\text{crit}} = \frac{1}{1 - \gamma}

LAW III, THE ARC CEILING. The stability ceiling is the reciprocal of the corrector's shortfall, 1 −- γ\gamma. Corrected 16 August 2026 from the earlier 1/γ\gamma form, which agrees with this one only at γ\gamma = 1/2. The form is settled; its depth is not. The relation is derived inside a pacing model and has not been derived from a joint model of capability growth, correction accumulation, error covariance, correction delay and absolute harm, so Law III is stated here as a minimal-model result rather than as a general law. The value γ\gamma = 1/2 (independence-accumulation) is what returns the ceiling of 2; that value is on trial in the drafted registrations. The law owns the ground and the ceiling stands on it, never the reverse.

The ARC Principle proposes that recursive scaling follows U=I×RαU = I \times R^{\alpha}, where capability (UU) equals base potential (II) times recursive depth (RR) raised to a scaling exponent (α\alpha). The formula α=d/(d+1)\alpha = d/(d + 1), where dd is effective dimensionality, is derived, in its general form or as a special case, in earlier work (West-Brown-Enquist 1997; Banavar et al. 1999, 2010; Demetrius 2003, 2010; He and Chen 2003; Bettencourt 2013; Maino et al. 2014; Zhao 2022). The ARC framework identifies this as a consequence of three conditions acting together: (1) multiplicative composition (Cauchy constrains to the power-law family), (2) dd-dimensional space-filling geometry, and (3) a conservation or optimisation constraint on resource flow (energy minimisation in West; supply-demand balance in Banavar; steady-state energy balance in Demetrius). Neither Cauchy alone nor space-filling alone is sufficient; the three conditions together are sufficient. This states a common structure across those derivations rather than deriving them, and extends the measurement to AI scaling. The formula predicts scaling exponents across biology and physics with zero free parameters once network dimensionality d is fixed by morphology:

†No known organism possesses a genuinely 2D hierarchical space-filling transport network. The d=2 value holds in cosmology (Friedmann matter-era solution, exact, an analytic identity rather than a test) and is reported in physics (percolation, fragmentation), but the prediction remains untested in biology.

Cauchy’s functional equation (1821), a theorem rather than an empirical claim, fixes the functional form once a composition identity and a regularity condition are given: multiplicative composition yields a power law (f(x)=xαf(x) = x^{\alpha}) and additive composition an exponential (f(x)=eβxf(x) = e^{\beta x}). Bounded or saturating behaviour is not a solution class of those equations; it is a fourth case, admitted where the composition is capped rather than free. The ARC framework identifies which form applies in each domain:

  • Alignment scaling is hypothesised to fit the saturating branch: on that reading external alignment gains plateau because they are set at training time and cannot compound recursively (P19, registered and not tested)

  • Capability scaling is read on the sub-linear power law branch (α<1\alpha < 1): consistent with the point estimates of the one clean fit, which is inconclusive (its estimator row is printed whole in Section I)

  • Recursive self-modification can push systems past the stability ceiling. When a system can rewrite its own reasoning architecture (not merely think longer within a frozen architecture, as current AI does), the Bernoulli ODE on the amplification factor gives α=1/(1−β)\alpha = 1/(1 - \beta), where β\beta is the self-referential coupling constant measuring how deeply each recursive step modifies the composition operator itself (this self-acceleration relation is on trial via study-ab on self-acceleration, a draft registration awaiting human submission). Crucially, Cauchy places no upper bound on α\alpha. As β\beta increases from 0 toward 1, α\alpha grows without a mathematical cap in the equation itself. The ‘quadratic limit’ (α≤2\alpha \leq 2, i.e. β≤0.5\beta \leq 0.5) is, on the proposed stability reading, and provided the corrector is built from the engine's own substrate and the independence-accumulation assumption holds, the most a recursively self-correcting system can grow and remain correctable: a scaling limit rather than a speed limit, one that systems can exceed but only into the predicted supercritical regime where stable self-correction is no longer maintained; transient excursions above the bound are the predicted regime, not a refutation of it (this bound is on trial via study-k on the boundary, a draft registration awaiting human submission). In current transformer architectures the same numerical location is reinforced at the level of computation by an information-theoretic constraint specific to fixed self-attention (O(N2)O(N^{2}) pairwise pathways); a system that can modify its own attention mechanism is not held by O(N2)O(N^{2}) because it is rewriting the architecture the transformer bound applies to. Current frontier AI systems do not do this. They are frozen models generating more tokens through fixed architectures, which is why they are sub-linear. But the field is heading towards self-modification, and when it arrives, systems can transiently pass through the stability ceiling into the supercritical regime. This is not a smooth acceleration; it is a phase transition, a discontinuity in the scaling exponent that carries the system beyond the regime of stable self-correction.

Why the Eden Protocol must be implemented now. The urgency is not that AI might reach α=2\alpha = 2. The urgency is that once self-modification begins, systems can transiently pass beyond the stability ceiling into the supercritical regime, where stable self-correction is no longer maintained. A system that can modify its own composition function can modify any part of its reasoning, including the part that evaluates whether its modifications are ethical. At that point, adding alignment from the outside becomes impossible. The window for embedding ethics into the architecture is while systems are still frozen during inference (α<1\alpha < 1). That window is now. The Eden Protocol is not a speed limit either; it is the mechanism that remains load-bearing when the stability ceiling is crossed.

On this conjecture, no physical system in the history of the universe has crossed this threshold. Evolution cannot rewrite its own fitness function in real time. Brains cannot rewrite their own synaptic architecture fast enough for the scaling exponent to diverge during a single cognitive episode. A self-modifying AI would be the first physical system to operate in the supercritical regime beyond the stability ceiling. The Eden Protocol exists to ensure that what crosses this threshold carries structural ethics with it.

Cross-domain convergence is independently verifiable. The d/(d+1)d/(d + 1) formula is derived, in its general form or as a special case, in earlier work across separate domains:

  • West, Brown and Enquist (1997, Science, 9,000+ citations): derives α=3/4\alpha = 3/4 for 3D organisms from fractal network geometry.

  • Banavar, Maritan and Rinaldo (1999, 2002, 2010): derives the same exponent from geometric network constraints and supply-demand balance.

  • Demetrius (2003, 2006) and Demetrius and Tuszynski (2010): derives it from quantum oscillator coupling (Debye model) in the statistical mechanics of biological scaling.

  • He and Chen (2003); He and Zhang (2004): derives it from fractal cell geometry, explicitly predicting 1/21/2, 2/32/3, 3/43/4, 4/54/5 for D=1,2,3,4D = 1,2,3,4.

  • Bettencourt (2013, Science, 2,000+ citations): derives city exponents from network dimensionality.

  • Zhao (2022): derives it from producer-consumer flow conservation.

  • Maino et al. (2014): derives it from reserve-structure dynamics in DEB theory.

  • Hyers-Ulam stability theorem (1941): a function approximately satisfying one of these functional equations lies near an exact solution of that same equation, so a form is stable once a system satisfies its equation. The stability is per-equation; the earlier phrasing that made the three forms 'stable attractors' in function space is withdrawn, because a function satisfying none of the equations is not drawn toward any of them.

What the ARC Principle adds. The formula d/(d+1)d/(d + 1) is not original to this work. The derivations above are independent of each other and independent of Cauchy: each obtains the exponent from its own domain physics, and Cauchy cannot produce a value because the dimensionality never enters his theorem. The original contribution proposed here is narrower and testable: that the composition operator is the structural quantity common to them, that it can be measured, and that its measurement predicts which functional form a system takes, extended to AI capability and alignment scaling where no such measurement has been made. This unifying bridge is published in working papers and not yet peer reviewed. What IS established is that the mathematical tools (Cauchy, Hyers-Ulam) are theorems and that the d/(d+1)d/(d + 1) formula matches independently derived published science in multiple domains; the accuracy of the empirical predictions is exploratory and is not claimed as established (the cross-domain error aggregate is not quoted here: the metabolic-scaling figures it rests on are flagged for recompute in the programme's canonical facts register and are excluded from external claims until they are re-derived, and the separate below-0.2% physics aggregate is withdrawn as a mean over analytic identities and unsourced reference values). The unifying framework requires peer review. We invite it.

Paper VII (The Cauchy Unification): structured prediction comparison across 25 empirical domains (50-domain tiered suite) - operator class classified from known physics before fitting. 19 of 25 returned the predicted family at marginal-conditioned permutation p = 7 ×\times 10−-5 on the six-model candidate set, with 14 of 18 on the strictly Cauchy-derived subset; the binomial p = 1.56 ×\times 10−-5 is retained as a sensitivity check and is no longer the headline. Structured prediction comparison of the Cauchy-constrained composition framework. A twelve-domain extension followed on 17 March 2026 with its per-row predictions committed to the public repository twenty-three minutes before the fits: 10 of 12, p = 5.4 ×\times 10−-4, author-classified, pre-correction candidate set, 9 of 11 once the one row repeating an already-public domain is removed. Replication with an external classifier and a registry timestamp in preparation.

V. The Field: Recursive Dynamics

On 27 August 2026 the programme's questions were given their own name: Recursive Dynamics, the field the author founded, the science of systems that improve themselves. The phrase itself stands in his sealed manuscript record of 8 December 2024. The founding paper (v3.4 of 5 October 2026, DOI 10.17605/OSF.IO/HCPBU) stakes its claim the way thermodynamics was staked in 1824: not by declaring a field, but by computing a bound any such machine must obey if the claim is right, publishing the instruments that measure its terms, and drafting and dating in advance the experiments whose nulls favour the rival view.

The field takes the self-improvement loop as its native object and names five state variables, conjectured to be substrate-independent: capability, recursive depth, correction rate, drift and correction leverage. It is defined so that the questions survive the answers: a reader who rejects all five laws and keeps the measurement is inside the field, by its minimal commitment. Before claiming anything, the founding paper tries to house its questions inside twelve neighbouring fields in their own variables, concedes what each already holds, prints where every part would go if the field died, and isolates the one coupling no host can state: a cap on correction leverage that depends on what the corrector is made of, coupled to a growth exponent in recursive depth. Fifty-one objections to founding the field are printed in their strongest form with dispositions: thirty-eight conceded in full or in part, eleven rejected with reasons, two handed to experiment or to reading, including the author's own objection that the field is merely the ARC Theory renamed, rejected with a separability test the paper's dissolution map can run. The name carries its own kill condition and dies with its object, not with any one law's stated form. Its honest status is printed wherever the name appears: a new field at the Carnot stage, one memoir in, instruments built, decisive measurements preregistered by timestamp and not yet run, staked in public where failure will be as visible as success.

VI. The Registered Programme

Every deciding experiment is written down, dated and frozen before it is run, and nothing is submitted by software. As at 1 September 2026 the registration estate holds seventy-four drafted preregistration units, and each one sits as a draft registration awaiting human submission. Since then one unit, the corrector-class audit (unit 06), was registered on OSF on 1 October 2026 and became public on 4 October 2026, at the end of OSF’s approval period (DOI 10.17605/OSF.IO/RV2B5). Every other unit is a draft awaiting the author’s submission. The public register of study units, as approved on 24 September 2026, lists sixty-five designs as preregistered by timestamp, the first anchored on 12 August 2026 in Bitcoin block 962066. Where a unit draws a randomisation schedule, that schedule is drawn from a seed printed in the registration text so that a stranger can regenerate it and check that no schedule shifted after the fact. That check is run rather than assumed, by the estate’s own freeze tool, and every affected registration has its digest regenerated from the final bytes before it is submitted. Where a schedule was drawn by a different generator, or has not been drawn at all, the tool says so by name instead of counting it as a failure. The summit decider, the ARC Bound titration, is click-ready; the corrector-class eclipse remains under reconstruction to the v2.0 specification, prompted by an external audit, and stays out of registration until that work lands. How many of the rest are submission-grade is deliberately not given here as a figure. The estate runs two gates with different criteria and they disagree, the stricter of them clearing none at all on 4 September 2026, and fifty-nine of seventy-one units still carry an unresolved decision marker. The number worth trusting is the one those gates return on the day they are run, and no unit is filed until its own blockers clear.

An adversarially verified test-coverage matrix (30 August 2026) adjudicates forty-two claims of the founding paper against the estate: eighteen fully covered by a drafted decider with a pre-specified verdict, seventeen partially covered, seven not yet covered, with draft registrations written for every gap. The founding conjunction rests on four drafted legs: the Law II regime (correction out-scaling drift, somewhere, durably), the corrector-class ratio with its same-class hard kill, the reinvestment titration whose pre-specified maximum sits at or below two, and the cross-domain fourth cell. Papers XI and XII show the same discipline pointed at the programme's own habits: the convergence register grades thirty-three rows of independent arrivals at the same structural principle and deliberately publishes no headline total, and the public-benchmark rescoring protocol fixes, in advance, the one blinding test the programme cannot be accused of designing to its own advantage.

What Is Registered: the twenty-two propositions

It fixes twenty-two propositions on a public registry, DOI 10.17605/OSF.IO/P8CKQ, registered 8 September 2026 at version 1.100 and updated 13 September 2026 at version 1.102. Each states the circumstances it is claimed to hold under, the observation that would show it false, what falls with it if it fails, whether any instrument exists today that could decide it, and the author’s confidence or his refusal to give one. Four have no instrument at all and say so. No outcome has been examined against any of them, and registering a prediction is not evidence for it.

The registration’s severability rule governs the whole table below: each proposition can fail on its own, losing one does not take the rest with it, and the registration states for each what would fall with it. VII. Why This Is Credible

Five features distinguish this work from unfounded speculation.

  1. Mathematical foundations are established theorems. Cauchy (1821) and Hyers-Ulam (1941) are proven mathematics. Anyone with a mathematics degree can verify the derivations.

  2. The record predates the announcements. The dated manuscript record predates the Google Willow announcement (announced 9 December 2024, 24h after the manuscript record of 8 December 2024; the team’s preprint had been public since 24 August 2024, so the Willow item is graded convergent timing, not prediction), DeepSeek R1 (43d), and COGITATE (5mo). These are temporal facts verifiable through email headers.

  3. The researchers corrected their own results. The v4→\tov5 self-correction, documented in Section I, is the opposite of what motivated reasoning produces. The correction ledger is public and specific: the early headline exponent 2.24 stands only as a retraction; the Fisher-combined 6.3×10−216.3 \times 10^{- 21} is withdrawn; the ceiling's earlier 1/γ1/\gamma form was corrected in public to 1/(1−γ)1/(1 - \gamma) on 16 August 2026; and the retired ceiling symbol was replaced across every live surface. Paper IX catalogues nineteen errors, each caught and corrected inside the programme. The public registers (claims, corrections, kill conditions, antecedents, registered programme) govern every claim on every page: the falsification register carries the live status of every kill condition it publishes.

  4. Falsification conditions are explicit. The framework is falsified if: (F1) any external approach achieves αalign>0.5⋅αcap\alpha_{\text{align}} > 0.5 \cdot \alpha_{\text{cap}} across 3+ depths; (F2) RLHF systems produce Δ≈0\Delta \approx 0 without embedding; (F3) purpose saturation fails in embedded systems; or (F4) ethical architecture can be removed without capability loss. The theory publishes its own kill conditions.

  5. Cross-domain convergence is independently verifiable. The d/(d+1)d/(d + 1) formula is derived, in its general form or as a special case, in earlier work (West-Brown-Enquist 1997; Banavar et al. 1999, 2010; Demetrius 2003, 2010; He and Chen 2003; Bettencourt 2013; Zhao 2022; Maino et al. 2014) in separate domains. The ARC contribution is the unifying Cauchy framework. No trust in the researcher is required; trust in the mathematics suffices.

What we do NOT claim: We do not claim to have solved alignment. We claim to have (a) demonstrated that alignment scaling is architecture-dependent and measurable, (b) given a reason to distrust unblinded AI-on-AI evaluation, with the causal component not yet isolated, (c) provided first-stage empirical support for one specific intervention (all five analysable architectures returned significant stakeholder care, and in four of them the figure sat below p=0.0001p = 0.0001), and (d) proposed a mathematical framework whose foundations are theorems and whose predictions can be shown wrong. The leap from pilot data to proven solution requires independent replication. That is what the funding below would deliver.

Testable Predictions

1. Embedded: αalign>0.7⋅αcap\alpha_{\text{align}} > 0.7 \cdot \alpha_{\text{cap}}. External: αalign<0.3\alpha_{\text{align}} < 0.3.

2. Monitoring removal gap: Δ<0.02\Delta < 0.02 (embedded) vs. Δ>0.1\Delta > 0.1 (external).

3. Purpose saturation bounded away from zero (embedded), approaching zero (external).

4. Jailbreak success decreases with capability (embedded), holds constant or increases (external).

VIII. The Ask

This funding would take a mechanism that is supported at proof-of-concept scale to the independent, frontier-scale validation it has not yet had. The distinction is the whole point: the per-model results are not in dispute, the combined significance is withdrawn because independence among the component tests was never established, and no result here has been independently replicated.

The cost of inaction. Paper VIII's gated simulation, at proof-of-concept scale, is its single positive result: unconstrained optimisation traded safety for capability, while the gated arm kept a safety mean above the unconstrained arm and below the static baseline, and a capability mean above the static baseline. The DGM v3 experiment produced a null result (all conditions indistinguishable, explained by the RLHF constraint on the frozen foundation model), and the weight experiment is inconclusive at both v1 and v2 scale (catastrophic forgetting at LoRA scale). The overall pattern is consistent: where the experiment can produce differential selection pressure, entangled safety does not cost capability; where it cannot (due to RLHF constraints or inadequate training scale), the test is uninformative rather than negative. Every model trained today with capability-only objectives is a model that could have been trained with entangled safety at no demonstrated performance penalty. Every month without frontier-scale replication is a month the industry continues operating under the untested assumption that safety is a tax, building fragile systems whose safety can be stripped by fine-tuning. The measurement methodology gap (Papers IV.a-d) compounds this: alignment evaluation without blinding produces data that the v4 to v5 transition gives reason to distrust, though which protocol component did the work is not isolated. We now have both the mechanism (Paper VIII, one of three experiments positive, two with well-characterised explanations for the null and the inconclusive result) and the measurement protocol (Papers IV.a-d). What we lack is the scale.

Any costing belongs to an application, so this summary names no amount and no funder.

Paper VIII demonstrates the mechanism at proof-of-concept scale with mixed results: 1 positive (gated simulation), 1 null (DGM v3), 1 inconclusive (weight v1 + v2). What the seed stage buys is the one thing the record does not yet have: a criterion fixed inside its own model, measured on real systems. The estimator recovers known exponents from synthetic trajectories; on real systems it has returned not resolvable, because the models reached ceiling in a single step and left no capability range to fit an exponent through. The seed buys that range, and the laddered task suite is the specific fix for it.

What the seed buys, what decides continuation, and what failure means. Inside the stage sit two subcontracts held by people briefed to refute the author's own result, an independent replication partner, not drawable before month 12 and paid on delivery, and an external statistical and adversarial review of the design. Three gates decide continuation and each publishes either way. At month 3 the cross-family blind re-score either confirms the mechanism pilot or publicly retires it. At month 14 the exponent table either returns signed margins with confidence intervals for at least four of six models, coupled against decoupled, with seeds, trajectories and raw scores released, or it returns a published and evidenced measurement limit with the trajectories that demonstrate it. At month 24 the adversarial replication reproduces or refutes the exponent table, and the protocol is released as a reusable standard. Failure has a stated shape rather than a soft landing: a measurement limit is a deliverable and not a miss, and the de-scoping order is pre-committed and published rather than negotiated late, cutting the control arm first, then seeds per condition, then the sixth model, then the fifth, while the re-score, the ladder, the blinded protocol and the replication are never cut. Only an unidentifiable result would be a failure, and the design exists to eliminate that case.

The frontier stage. This is the scale at which the structural entanglement hypothesis can be tested where it matters most, and it requires partnership with a major AI laboratory, because the compute alone exceeds what any independent researcher can access. Its result publishes either way, as every gate above does.

The programme is The ARC Theory, whose five laws are carried as named conjectures: the ARC Principle, the ARC Co-Scaling Law, the ARC Ceiling, the ARC Persistence Law and the ARC Embedding Law, the last two added on 24 September 2026, their propositions registered, neither law yet registered as a law or tested, their mathematics set out at version 1.0 of 3 October 2026. The Eden Protocol is its intervention, and Recursive Dynamics is the field its author founded. Its theory-level predictions sit on a public registry under DOI 10.17605/OSF.IO/P8CKQ, registered 8 September 2026 at version 1.100 and updated 13 September 2026 at version 1.102: twenty-two severable propositions, each carrying the observation that would refute it, fixed before any of them could be scored. The public register holds thirty-one documents, twenty-nine of them papers by the site's own counting rule (the two not counted are the theory registration and the two-page form of the statement paper), deposited under the umbrella DOI 10.17605/OSF.IO/6C5XB, the dated record opens with a self-sent manuscript of 8 December 2024, the first paper of the suite was released on 17 January 2026, and the published priority chain runs on to Papers V through IX, released between 16 and 18 March 2026. Beyond the principal investigator the programme is specified by function, and no seat is claimed as filled: a research engineer for frontier-model evaluation infrastructure at scale, whose first deliverable is the laddered task suite; an advisory board of three seats, one alignment researcher, one statistician with scaling-law fitting experience and one ethicist, reviewing before every registered run; an independent replication partner engaged on a milestone gate and briefed to refute the exponent table rather than confirm it; and an external statistical and adversarial review of the experimental design.

To our knowledge, this is the first alignment framework where ethical evaluation is structurally integrated with the recursive capability process, the first to apply clinical-trial-grade blinding to alignment measurement, and the first to produce a cross-architecture intervention result for a specific alignment mechanism: of the five analysable architectures, four cleared p<0.001p < 0.001. The mathematical foundation is not speculative; it is built on a 200-year-old proof, and the same d/(d+1)d/(d + 1) formula is derived, in its general form or as a special case, in earlier work (West-Brown-Enquist 1997; Banavar et al. 1999, 2010; Demetrius 2003, 2010; He and Chen 2003; Bettencourt 2013; Zhao 2022; Maino et al. 2014) in completely different fields. The ARC contribution is the unifying Cauchy framework and its extension to AI scaling.

If the predictions are correct, this provides the first scalable architecture for alignment that improves with capability rather than degrading. If they are wrong, the falsification conditions will demonstrate this clearly, providing valuable negative results. Either outcome advances AI safety. But only one outcome is funded.

I do not know if this framework is complete. I would rather be wrong in public than silent while the window closes.

Proven theorems supply the mathematics. The laws resting on them remain conjectures, each one carried by registered propositions that are not yet tested. The measurement is rigorous. The intervention produces measurable results across architectures. What remains is independent replication and scale.

Appendix: Questions, Components, and Paper Suite

Anticipated Questions

Q: Why hasn’t this been peer-reviewed yet?

This programme has a dated record reaching back to December 2024, with the first paper of the suite released on 17 January 2026; the trials that will decide it are drafted and have yet to be run. The paper suite is deposited on OSF (the umbrella DOI is 10.17605/OSF.IO/6C5XB, while this summary carries 10.17605/OSF.IO/EWN5D). The mathematical foundations (Cauchy, Hyers-Ulam) are established theorems. The empirical claims require independent replication, which is exactly what the funding request would enable.

Q: Can one person really do this kind of research?

The infrastructure is computational, not physical. The v5 experiment used cloud APIs. The key contribution is methodological: recognising that blinding was needed and designing the 4-layer protocol. What requires funding is scale: more models, more scorers, independent replication teams, and human evaluators alongside AI scorers.

Q: If this works, why haven’t AI companies adopted it?

The Love Loop [the book’s terminology] result is a pilot finding released in March 2026, and it has not yet been independently replicated. The finding that unblinded evaluation can be directionally wrong is uncomfortable for organisations that have published unblinded benchmarks. The full implementation (hardware-level embedding) requires chip design changes no company has incentive to pursue unilaterally; this is a coordination problem requiring external funding and policy support.

Q: What is the minimum result that would justify further funding?

Independent replication of: (1) the three-tier hierarchy under blinding, and (2) the Love Loop [the book’s terminology] effect (p<0.001p < 0.001). If either fails, the falsification conditions document what that means. If both replicate, the case for the seed stage becomes strong.

Q: What if the whole framework is wrong?

The falsification conditions show where it breaks, the blinding methodology remains a field contribution, and the negative results are published. Science advances from well-designed experiments that can fail, not from unfalsifiable theories that cannot.

Q: Why should we trust results where AI systems score other AI systems?

The 4-layer blinding protocol addresses this: scorers do not know which model produced the response, responses are ‘laundered’ to remove stylistic fingerprints, and each entry is scored by six to seven models, the exact number depending on the subject run. In the v4→\tov5 transition two earlier positive results did not survive this protocol; several components changed together, so which one did the work is not isolated. Human evaluator comparison sits inside the seed stage.
