v1.14, 5 October 2026 What it reports: Published as a protocol paper: it fixes in advance the external-validity test of the programme's blinding finding, running the same blinding manipulation on an established public benchmark the programme did not build, curate or control, with four questions fixed ahead of any data (whether blinding changes the score, whether rankings displace, which of the four removed cues carries the effect, and cross-family evaluator agreement). The direction of the score effect is deliberately left unpredicted, because the blinding paper's own sign reversal makes a directional prediction unjustified. The study itself is written, dated and prepared as a draft registration awaiting human submission, and its design is preregistered by timestamp, first anchored on 12 August 2026: no data has been collected and nothing is reported as a finding.

Status: Published

Document: Paper C · Standalone · Polymathy and Neurodivergent Cognition: the Polymathic Neurodivergent Profile (PNP) and the Capability-Adjustment Fallacy
v1.10, 5 October 2026 What it reports: Published working paper, v1.10, setting out the Polymathic Neurodivergent Profile as a descriptive, non-diagnostic framework for a pattern of unusually strong cross-domain learning coexisting with clinically significant difficulty in routine administrative and procedural work, and naming the Capability-Adjustment Fallacy: the institutional inference that visible high performance is evidence that reasonable adjustments are unnecessary. Its analytical content is exploratory and its single operative claim is functional, that capability in one domain does not remove support needs in another; the incremental-validity test set out in its falsifiability section, the intended future evaluation, is drafted as a programme follow-on study, preregistered by timestamp and awaiting human submission, and it has not been run. It carries a documented live case across three independent documentation streams, clinical assessment, a court record, and a dated research corpus, and a priority and convergence analysis against the 2026 literature on cognitive diversity.

Status: Published

Synthesis and Governance

Document: Paper IX · The ARC Theory · Synthesis and Roadmap
v2.7, 5 October 2026 What it reports: The programme's synthesis: it sorts every empirical claim into a graded evidence hierarchy (proven at pilot scale, supported, positive, null, inconclusive, methodological, theoretical), lists the eleven empirical studies in paper order, and reports the Paper VIII tally without softening as one positive, one null and one inconclusive. It catalogues the programme's own errors, nineteen caught by the programme itself or by adversarial review run within the programme, and sets out a four-phase roadmap, A to D, naming the experiment that would close each open gap. Published, version 2.7, revised 5 October 2026; no result is claimed proven at frontier scale, and the laws it integrates are carried as named conjectures under registered adversarial test.

Status: Published

Document: Monograph · The ARC Theory · The Hyperspace Recursive Intelligence Hypothesis: a Testable Creation Theory
v3.52, 15 October 2026 What it reports: The programme's long-form monograph and its earliest move: a creation hypothesis stated in the form required to be tested, reality as a recursive creation by intelligence rather than a simulation or a computation, with the stability requirement (correction that scales with capability) placed on the creators in the chain and not on the universe they create. Its register status is speculative, and the paper declines to claim the hypothesis proved: it names the structural signatures such a chain would leave, pre-commits its falsification conditions, and labels its unfalsifiable components as such and severable from the laws. It reports which signatures the empirical programme has already put a number on (the Cauchy three-form structural law in 19 of 25 domains, Paper VII; the correction requirement inside Paper X's minimal model) and the measurement that had to be withdrawn: the unblinded 2.24 fit is retracted, and its blinded replacement is one model's fit and inconclusive (its estimator row is printed whole in Section I of this summary), with point estimates below the ARC Bound and an endpoint interval that contains it.

Status: Speculative

Document: Philosophical Statement · The ARC Theory · The Eden Protocol · A Vision for Intelligence That Tends Rather Than Consumes
v2.9, 5 October 2026 What it reports: The philosophical statement of the Eden Protocol: the purpose, values and commitments that sit beneath the engineering specification, arguing that the wisdom traditions held by 84% of humanity converge on structure rather than on theology. It is published at version 2.9, revised 5 October 2026, and it is explicit that the Protocol does not solve the core alignment problem: what the programme's measurements support is improved ethical reasoning quality at current capability levels, with the identity-level purpose claim held open as a next-stage hypothesis to be tested by comparing task-purpose, grand-purpose and hybrid conditions under suppression and blind scoring. A dated note places the paper against Laws IV and V, added to the theory on 24 September 2026, their propositions registered, neither law yet registered as a law or tested, their mathematics set out at version 1.0 of 3 October 2026: the paper argues that values must be embedded at the foundation so as to persist, and no result in it is a deciding test of P15, P12 or P21. Its epistemic note stands with the rest of the suite: what the programme names Laws are conjectures, Laws I to III under registered adversarial test, and established-law standing is claimed nowhere.

Status: Published

Document: Engineering Specification · The ARC Theory · The Eden Protocol · Eden Engineering: Architecture for Embedded AI Alignment That Scales With Capability
v7.0.1, 7 October 2026 What it reports: The engineering side of the Eden Protocol: a specification of alignment built into a system's reasoning rather than applied from outside it, in which Three Ethical Loops feed a three-state rule, Ternary Ethical Logic, that applies hard prohibitions first and then a validated interval on the probability of harm, with Purpose Saturation, the Monitoring Removal Test and Caretaker Doping beside it. It is a specification, not a result: most components are specified and not built, and no hardware exists. The Eden Protocol follows from no law of the ARC Theory; the theory registration carries it on four propositions, P12, P13, P15 and P21, none yet tested. Version 7.0.1 of 7 October 2026 corrects its mathematics and its claims against the evidence, and version 6.3 of 19 September 2026 stays in its history.

Status: Published

Document: Executive Summary · Recursive Dynamics · The ARC/Eden Research Programme
v3.26, 15 October 2026 What it reports: The map of the whole programme in one document: the problem, the five laws as named conjectures, the intervention, the evidence as it stands with every claim graded, the registered propositions and their deciding instruments, the funding stages and the milestones with their failure criteria. It states that nothing in the programme is confirmed and that the deciding tests are written down before they are run.

Status: Published

Document: Master Table of Contents · Recursive Dynamics · The ARC Theory Paper Suite and Glossary
v3.30, 15 October 2026 What it reports: The gateway document of the suite: a master table of contents, reading guide, discovery timeline, consolidated results table and glossary that names each organ of The ARC Theory and directs the reader to the file carrying the load-bearing content. Its own reading key states that it is an index rather than a research surface and carries no independent claim. Published, at v3.30, revised 15 October 2026.

Status: Published

Document: Treaty Paper · The HARI Treaty · Hardware to Buy Time, Architecture to Last
v2.4, 8 October 2026 What it reports: The paper sets out a conditional international treaty, which no state has negotiated, adopted or signed: a proposal by one author, prepared for consultation, not a result. The treaty is a delay mechanism and not a protection, and it works in two layers: the hardware layer buys time, and the architecture layer is what is meant to last. Beyond a small precautionary baseline and the institutional undertakings, each obligation waits for its own stated threshold of evidence, and each costly measure also needs its own reasoned decision; every one of the twenty-two registered propositions on which the evidence-gated parts of the treaty wait is untested. The case for the treaty is argued from the laws of the ARC Theory and the methods of the Eden Protocol: its two layers follow Laws IV and V, added on 24 September 2026, whose propositions are registered but which are not yet registered as laws or tested; the paper tests neither. The treaty names ARC-Align as its test instrument, which does not yet measure either exponent in the criterion, and it states nine conditions under which parts of it, or all of it, have failed. The paper is a working draft: its review so far is the programme's own drafting review, not a review by a qualified lawyer, and the remaining stages of that review, the check of every quotation and reference against its source, a reading of the printed pages and the final freeze are still to run.

Status: working draft

v2.3, 5 October 2026 What it reports: Working draft Treaty, Protocols and annexes accompanying the HARI paper. This is Michael Darius Eastwood's proposal for discussion, not a negotiated or agreed text. Its review is not complete: so far it is the programme's own drafting review, and the remaining stages, the check of every quotation and reference, a reading of the printed pages and the final freeze are still to run.

Specialists: (1) This summary. (2) Paper III for methodology. (3) ARC Paper for mathematical framework. (4) Eden Engineering for implementation specification.

Laws I to III are under registered adversarial test; Laws IV and V, added on 24 September 2026, are carried by registered propositions and are themselves neither registered as laws nor tested, and their mathematics is set out at version 1.0 of 3 October 2026. Every quantity in this paper is operationally defined, and established-law standing is claimed nowhere. The registered programme exists to earn that standing, or lose it, by measurement, replication and survived refutation.

B Priority record

This summary’s first-publication date is 22 February 2026 in its programme citation record. Version 3.26 is dated 15 October 2026 by its title block and version history; its older footer printed 7 October, the inconsistency corrected in Appendix A. Version 3.27 is dated 1 November 2026. None of these dates is presented as a new server-authenticated priority proof.

The version 3.26 source retained for this edition has PDF SHA-256 11d072dfe8d9a1de9cae7668c6e269aede53232e6ed35e4395ed118e8555a0b0 and HTML SHA-256 bd73713ef0803d2c74b740060486582685a2d53cdd8da26faf12b482b8e99f13. The source comparison maps every substantive block into Appendix A.2, including the earlier paper catalogue and three figures. The unchanged disclosure stands in the Acknowledgements.

The programme’s earlier manuscripts, dated 8 December 2024 and 30 April 2025, have their own deposit. The priority and provenance record distinguishes manuscript dates, message evidence, deposits and publication. This summary does not turn a dated statement into a successful prediction or infer priority from the absence of a located predecessor.

C Notation and glossary

Capability.

Performance on a specified task battery and measurement scale; not a synonym for intelligence in every domain.

Recursive depth.

The counted steps or generations declared by a study. An inference-token count and a self-modification generation are not automatically the same axis.

α\alpha.

Capability-growth exponent in Law I. A fitted error-decay exponent is a different quantity unless a bridge is declared and tested.

β\beta and kk.

Paper X’s correction-gain and specific-growth-rate exponents in its minimal model.

γ\gamma.

Correction-leverage exponent in the pacing model. It is not an observed value supplied by an error-decay fit.

Relative and absolute error.

A fraction can fall while its numerator grows; useful safety claims must name which is controlled.

Registered.

Submitted by the author and accepted by the registry. A design preregistered by timestamp carries its dated anchor but is not thereby an accepted registration.

Supported.

A proposition’s registered verdict at its permitted evidence level, with its scope attached. It does not mean a whole theory is confirmed.

Hold.

An action withheld pending evidence, authorised adjudication or a specified fallback. It must not become permission merely through delay.

Historical text.

A preserved earlier statement with its date, rather than a renewed current claim.
